data.value: Each of these is a collection of its own, with its own reading position. Where the editors state which part there corresponds to what you have read here, you can go on there from that part – by your own choice.

data.name: Account_Lead
data.value: An account is yours on every device: your list and how far you have read follow you. It asks for a name, a mail address and a password – nothing else about you.

data.name: Account_NeedsHttps
data.value: A password does not travel in the open: the account is reached over https only.

data.name: Account_Name_Hint
data.value: 3 to 40 characters: letters, digits, spaces, dots and hyphens. Others will see this name; it need not be your real one.

data.name: Account_Password_Hint
data.value: At least 12 characters. A sentence of your own is a good password.

data.name: Account_Register_Privacy
data.value: The site keeps the name, the mail address and a value derived from the password – never the password itself. Nobody else sees the address, and the site writes to it only about the account. If you lose the password, a link mailed to the address or one of your recovery codes lets you in again.

data.name: Account_Recover_Lead
data.value: One of your recovery codes lets you choose a new password – the way in when you cannot read the mail of your address any more.

data.name: Account_Reopen_Lead
data.value: A closed account is kept for 30 days. Until then its name or mail address and its password open it again.

data.name: Account_Codes_Lead
data.value: Write these down now and keep them in a safe place: they are shown this once. If you lose the password, each of them lets you in one time.

data.name: Account_CodesLeft
data.value: Recovery codes you have not used yet: {0}.

data.name: Account_Password_Note
data.value: With another password, every other device is signed out.

data.name: Account_NewCodes_Lead
data.value: Get new codes. The ones you have are worth nothing afterwards.

data.name: Account_Close_Lead
data.value: Closing signs you out everywhere at once. After 30 days the account and everything that belongs to it is deleted for good; until then its name and password open it again.

data.name: Account_Said_recovered

data.name: Account_Said_password

data.name: Account_Said_codes
data.value: These are your new recovery codes.

data.name: Account_Said_closed
data.value: Your account is closed. It will be deleted for good in 30 days.

data.value: A password has at most 1000 characters.

data.name: Account_Problem_wrong-closed

data.value: Pages your list does not have yet are added. A reading position is taken only for a collection your account has none for – what your account says is never moved. The device keeps what it holds.

data.name: Account_Register_Adopts
data.value: What this device holds – your list and how far you have read – goes into the new account.

data.name: Account_Invite_Lead
data.value: An invitation is a link. You pass it on yourself, or the site mails it to an address you name. It makes an account for one person and nothing else: no connection between the two of you follows from it. It can be used for 14 days.

data.name: Account_Invited
data.value: You were invited to Dastan. Make your account here.

data.name: Account_Invitation_Gone
data.value: This invitation can no longer be used. You can make an account all the same.

data.name: Account_Said_brought
data.value: What this device held is in your account now.

data.name: Account_Said_invited
data.value: The invitation is made. Pass its link on to the person you invite.

data.name: Account_Problem_invitations
data.value: You have 10 invitations that can still be used. Take one back, or wait until one is used or runs out.

data.name: Saved_Where_Account
data.value: Your list is kept with your account and is the same on every device you sign in on. It holds at most 200 pages.

data.name: Saved_Where_Offer
data.value: With an account your list follows you to every device.

data.name: People_Page_Link
data.value: Your page as others see it

data.value: A relationship is something two people show together. One asks, the other accepts – nobody can accept for somebody else. It is shown to the two of you only, until each of you says who else may see it.

data.name: People_None
data.value: You show no relationship with anybody yet.

data.name: People_Shown_Note
data.value: Somebody else sees a relationship only when both of you allow them. What you choose here is your side of it.

data.name: People_Ask_Kind
data.value: What you are to each other

data.name: People_Ask_Note
data.value: They are told by mail, unless they turned that off, and find your request on their page. Nothing is shown to anybody until they accept, and to decline is their right. You can show several relationships with the same person – a friend who is a colleague too.

data.name: People_Said_asked
data.value: Your request is made. It waits for their answer.

data.name: People_Said_accepted
data.value: You accepted. It is shown to the two of you only, until you both choose otherwise.

data.name: People_Said_declined
data.value: You declined. Nothing is shown to anybody.

data.name: People_Said_ended
data.value: The relationship is ended. It is shown to nobody any more.

data.name: People_Said_circle-removed
data.value: The circle is removed. What was shown to it is shown to the two of you only.

data.name: People_Problem_later
data.value: That was asked too often. Please try again in an hour.

data.name: People_Problem_kind
data.value: Please choose what you are to each other.

data.name: People_Problem_exists
data.value: You two have this relationship, or a request for it, already.

data.name: People_Problem_declined-lately
data.value: This account declined a request of yours not long ago. You can ask again after 30 days.

data.name: People_Problem_too-many
data.value: 20 requests of yours wait for an answer. Take one back, or wait for an answer.

data.name: People_Problem_circle-name
data.value: A circle needs a name of 1 to 40 characters that you have not used yet, and you can have 20 circles.

data.name: People_Circles_Lead
data.value: A circle is a name for some of the people you show a relationship with – “Family”, “Close friends”. You can show a relationship to a circle instead of to everybody. Nobody is told that they are in a circle, and only you see its name.

data.name: People_Circle_Empty
data.value: Once somebody has accepted a relationship with you, you can put them into this circle.

data.name: Person_Lead_Self
data.value: This is your own page. Others see a relationship here only when both of you allow them.

data.name: Person_None
data.value: Nothing is shown to you here.

data.name: Trees_Lead
data.value: A family tree is yours. You say who else may see it and who may change it, and every change is kept with who made it. Nobody else sees it.

data.name: Trees_None
data.value: You have no family tree yet, and none is shared with you.

data.name: Trees_Shared_Editor
data.value: {0} lets you see and change this tree.

data.name: Trees_Add_Note
data.value: Only you see it until you name somebody.

data.name: Trees_Said_made
data.value: The tree is made. Add the first person below.

data.name: Trees_Said_renamed
data.value: The tree has its new name.

data.name: Trees_Said_person-removed
data.value: The record is removed, with its links.

data.name: Trees_Problem_tree-name
data.value: A tree needs a name of 1 to 80 characters, and you can own 20 trees.

data.value: A person needs a name of 1 to 80 characters. A year is a number from 1 to 9999, a month and a day are ones the calendar has, and nobody dies before they are born. Of somebody who lives a record says the year of birth and not the day – the day is theirs to say. A tree holds 500 people.

data.name: Trees_Problem_link-kind
data.value: Please choose what the two are to each other.

data.name: Trees_Problem_link-unknown
data.value: Both people have to be in this tree.

data.name: Trees_Problem_link-same
data.value: A link is between two different people.

data.name: Trees_Problem_link-exists
data.value: These two are linked already: two people hold one role in a family.

data.name: Trees_Problem_link-loop
data.value: That would make somebody their own ancestor.

data.name: Tree_People_None
data.value: Nobody is in this tree yet.

data.name: Tree_Person_Note
data.value: A record says little on purpose: a name and years. A person needs no account to be in a tree, and being in your tree gives you no say over who they are.

data.name: Tree_Links_Few
data.value: With two people in the tree you can link them.

data.name: Tree_Members_Title
data.value: Who may see or change this tree

data.name: Tree_Members_Lead
data.value: You can name people you show a relationship with. Who may change the tree adds, changes and removes people and links; only you name others, rename the tree or remove it.

data.name: Tree_Members_Nobody
data.value: Once somebody has accepted a relationship with you, you can name them here.

data.name: Tree_Remove_Lead
data.value: Remove this tree with everybody in it. This cannot be undone.

data.name: Tree_Claims_Note
data.value: Somebody says that a record you made is them. Confirm it only if you know it is so – the same name is not proof. Confirming names the account on the record and changes nothing else: nobody sees more than before.

data.name: Tree_Claim_Waits
data.value: You said this is you. It waits for the answer of who made the record.

data.name: Tree_Claim_NotMe
data.value: This is not me after all

data.name: Trees_Said_claimed
data.value: You said that this record is you. Who made the record will answer.

data.name: Trees_Said_claim-confirmed
data.value: Confirmed. The record names the account now.

data.name: Trees_Said_unclaimed
data.value: Taken back. The record names nobody.

data.name: Trees_Problem_claim-taken
data.value: This record is another account already.

data.name: Trees_Problem_claim-own
data.value: You are a record of this tree already, or have said so and wait for the answer.

data.name: Trees_Problem_claim-nobody
data.value: Somebody other than you has to confirm that a record is you, and for this record there is nobody: you made it yourself.

data.name: Account_Export_Lead
data.value: Get everything the site keeps about your account as one file: your list and reading positions, invitations, relationships and circles, the family trees you own, and your photographs by what you wrote about them (the pictures themselves are on the page of your photographs). Trees of others are named, not copied. No password is in it, and no code of an invitation that can still be used.

data.value: The family tree “{0}” as a drawing

data.name: Tree_Drawing_Note

data.name: Photos_None
data.value: You have brought in no photograph yet.

data.name: Photos_Add_Note

data.name: Photos_Said_approved

data.name: Photos_Problem_photo-large
data.value: The picture is larger than 10 MB.

data.name: Photos_Problem_photo-many
data.value: You have 200 photographs, which is as many as an account holds. Remove one first.

data.name: Photos_Problem_photo-file
data.value: The file is no PNG, JPEG or WebP image, or cannot be read as one.

data.name: PublicTree_Lead
data.value: A family tree somebody made public. Everybody living it names has agreed to be named here.

data.name: Tree_Publication_Lead
data.value: A public tree is seen by everybody, with or without an account: its people, their years and how they belong together – not who it is shared with and not its history. It needs the agreement of everybody living it names. Somebody who has no account cannot agree, so a tree that names a living person without an account cannot be public.

data.value: If something on this site is against the law, violates your rights or breaks the rules of the site, tell us here. Anybody can do this; you need no account.

data.name: Notice_How
data.value: A person reads every notice – no program decides. We look at it as soon as we can and decide whether the content stays, is hidden or is removed. If you give a mail address, we confirm that your notice arrived and tell you what we decided and what you can do if you disagree. Whoever posted the content is told the reasons when we restrict it, but not who gave the notice, unless the law requires it.
